title: Motor overload protection tripped
shortDescription: Mixer stops due to thermal protection.
fullDescription:
KitchenAid stand mixers (Pro 600, Artisan) include a thermal cutoff that stops the motor when overloaded. Heavy doughs or extended runtime trigger it.

Let the unit cool 30 minutes and reset.

title: Worm gear stripped
shortDescription: Sacrificial nylon worm gear teeth sheared.
fullDescription:
KitchenAid mixers use a sacrificial nylon worm gear designed to fail before the motor. Symptoms: motor runs but planetary doesn't move, grinding sound.

Replacement is straightforward but requires regreasing the gearbox.

fixSteps.title: Replace worm gear
fixSteps.instruction: Remove gearbox cover, swap worm gear, regrease.

faq.a: Pro 600 has metal gears - different repair.

title: Speed control board faulty
shortDescription: Speeds inconsistent or only one speed.
fullDescription: Speed control board uses phase control. Failures cause running at full speed only, not running at low, or sudden surges.

title: Grease leak from planetary
fullDescription:
Older KitchenAid mixers used a grease that thins at high temperatures and leaks past the planetary seal.

Clean and re-grease with food-safe grease.

fixSteps.title: Regrease
fixSteps.instruction: Disassemble head, clean old grease, repack with KitchenAid grease.

faq.a: Use KitchenAid-approved or NSF H1 grease.

title: Mixer will not turn on
shortDescription: Dead unit, no motor, no light.
fullDescription: Common causes: blown fuse, broken switch, or worn brushes that lost contact.

fixSteps.title: Replace brushes
fixSteps.instruction: Remove brush caps, install new carbon brushes.

title: Beater hits bowl or wobbles
fullDescription: Beater-to-bowl clearance is set by a screw on the head pivot. After heavy use it drifts. Adjust per KitchenAid procedure.

fixSteps.title: Adjust beater height
fixSteps.instruction: Use dime test - beater should just move dime.

title: Excessive noise from gearbox
fullDescription: Old grease, worn bearings, or stripped gear teeth cause noise. Regrease first; if persists, inspect gears.

title: Head tilts down during mixing
shortDescription: Locking lever fails to hold head.
fullDescription: Tilt-head models lock via a pin and lever. Worn locking pin or loose pivot screw causes head to drop.

fixSteps.title: Tighten pivot screw
fixSteps.instruction: Lift head, tighten central pivot screw.

title: Power hub attachment stuck
shortDescription: Cannot remove attachment from front hub.
fullDescription: Front power hub can seize from food residue or rust. Apply gentle heat or oil; do not force.

fixSteps.title: Penetrating oil
fixSteps.instruction: Apply, wait 20 min, gently work loose.

title: Burning odor during use
fullDescription: Burning smell during heavy mixing usually indicates worn brushes or stalled motor. Stop use and inspect.

title: Motor brushes worn
fullDescription: Carbon brushes need replacement. This is a common diagnostic indication on KitchenAid stand mixers. Most issues can be resolved with cleaning, reset, or part replacement following the brand's service procedure.

fixSteps.title: Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug stand mixer for 60 seconds, then plug back in.

fixSteps.title: Clean
fixSteps.instruction: Clean any sensors/contacts indicated by the brand's manual.

fixSteps.title: Test
fixSteps.instruction: Run a normal cycle and verify error does not return.

whenToCallPro: If problem persists after cleaning and reset, professional service may be needed.

faq.a: Resolve the error first to avoid worsening the issue.
If under warranty, contact manufacturer before DIY repair.
